key_insight: The paper introduces a quadrature-aware complex-linear boundary operator that predicts acoustic pressure fields from vibrating-surface excitation while enforcing complex superposition and zero-response physics by design.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster and more physically consistent surrogate modeling for resonant acoustics problems where repeated boundary-driven wave simulations are too costly.
method: Maps complex normal velocity on a source surface to complex receiver pressure using learned source/receiver bases with explicit surface-quadrature contraction.
Represents the source with coordinates, normals, and quadrature weights instead of a fixed flattened input vector to preserve linearity in the excitation.
Uses MRT lattice Boltzmann solver data in a solver-agnostic boundary-to-field format and benchmarks against a complex DeepONet baseline.
evidence_signal: Across five seeds, CLBO achieved mean complex relative field error 0.184 ± 0.00771 versus 0.367 ± 0.00742 for DeepONet, with source-superposition error 1.31 × 10^-7 and about 1.83 × 10^4× faster inference than the reference calculation.
watch_item: The strong gains depend on accurately known boundary quadrature and source geometry, so performance may degrade if source discretization or boundary representation is noisy or inconsistent.
paper_title: Quadrature-Aware Complex-Linear Neural Operator for Boundary-to-Field Prediction in Resonant Acoustics
